How do i unlink the GitHub Slack Integration just from DMs?
Select Topic Area
Question
The github bot integration on the Slack has a link button in its DM but does not have an unlink slash command. I've searched its settings for an hour with no luck.
How do i stop the GitHub bot from tagging my slack username in places, or better yet, just unlink the bot from my personal account, but still keep it in the slack workspace and all its slack channels.

predicted_answer: In Slack, run the slash command “/github signout” (for example in the DM with the GitHub app). That disconnects your GitHub account from your Slack user—mentions require you to be signed in, so signing out will stop the GitHub app from tagging your Slack username while leaving the app installed in the workspace.

Question
I have enrolled to the copilot annual subscription. Can I cancel the subscription while it is available, and will I get back the remaining payment?
predicted_answer: Yes — you can cancel an individual Copilot plan at any time and you’ll keep access until the end of your current billing cycle (you’ll be downgraded to Copilot Free afterwards). Whether you get money back depends on the plan: organization/seat licenses generally do not get refunds for unused time; under GitHub’s legacy annual Copilot Pro/Pro+ policy you could cancel an annual plan and receive a prorated refund (or prorated credit when switching to a monthly plan).

question:
Changing "Workflow permissions" to "Read and write"
Hello.
In my personal account I could successfully change the "Workflow permissions" from "Read" to "Read and write" (under Repo -> Settings -> Actions/General).
I just created a trial Enterprise. There, at organization or repo level, I cannot make the same change: the option "Read and write" is disabled with the message "Repository administrators will only be able to change the default permissions to a more restrictive setting".
How can I ensure to assign also write permissions to the workflows in my organizational repos?
Thank you
Stefano
task_description:
Changing "Workflow permissions" to "Read and write"
Hello.
In my personal account I could successfully change the "Workflow permissions" from "Read" to "Read and write" (under Repo -> Settings -> Actions/General).
I just created a trial Enterprise. There, at organization or repo level, I cannot make the same change: the option "Read and write" is disabled with the message "Repository administrators will only be able to change the default permissions to a more restrictive setting".
How can I ensure to assign also write permissions to the workflows in my organizational repos?
Thank you
Stefano
predicted_answer: The organization option is disabled because your Enterprise has a more restrictive default for the GITHUB_TOKEN; org settings inherit enterprise defaults and cannot select a more permissive setting. To enable write permissions for workflows in org repos either (1) as an Enterprise owner change the enterprise-level Actions default permissions to allow read & write (so organizations can select it), or (2) have a repository administrator with write access set the specific permissions in the workflow file (permissions: in the workflow) to grant write. Note also the “Send write tokens to workflows from pull requests” Actions setting affects whether write tokens are sent for PRs from forks.
